title: Texas Voters Hand Attorney General Office to Democrat After H-1B Probes
excerpt: Nathan Johnson's win puts the office that issued H-1B investigative demands to nearly 30 North Texas businesses under Democratic control for the first time since 1994, as Democrats also flip the Texas House.
body:
• Democrat Nathan Johnson defeated Republican Mayes Middleton for Texas attorney general with 52.4% of the vote in an Associated Press-called race, giving Democrats the office for the first time since 1994.
  • Democrats also won control of the 150-seat Texas House for the first time since the 2002 election cycle, while Republicans kept the state Senate, leaving divided government in Austin.
  • The office Johnson inherits in January ran the state's H-1B scrutiny drive under Ken Paxton, including civil investigative demands to nearly 30 North Texas businesses over suspected visa fraud and so-called ghost offices.
  • For Texas H-1B employers and workers: Johnson has not said whether he will continue those investigations, and a change of attorney general does not change federal H-1B rules, which remain with USCIS and the U.S. Department of Labor.

Texas voters have handed the state attorney general's office — the office that spent 2026 investigating H-1B employers across North Texas — to a Democrat for the first time in more than three decades, as part of a statewide sweep that also flipped the Texas House of Representatives.

Democrat Nathan Johnson, a Dallas state senator, defeated Republican Mayes Middleton, a state senator from Galveston. USA Today reported that Johnson received 52.4% of the vote to Middleton's 45.9% — 5,133,740 votes to 4,502,855 — in a race called by the Associated Press. The Texas Tribune reported that Middleton called Johnson to concede on election night. Democrats won every statewide race on the ballot: Gina Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott, James Talarico defeated outgoing Attorney General Ken Paxton for U.S. Senate, and Vikki Goodwin defeated Lieutenant Governor Dan Patrick. Republicans kept the Texas Senate, denying Democrats a full trifecta.

Democrats take the Texas House

Democrats took the Texas House for the first time since Republicans won it in the 2002 election. They entered election night with 62 of the chamber's 150 seats and needed to flip 14 for a majority, the Tribune reported via Bilkul Online. By Wednesday afternoon the Associated Press had called the chamber for Democrats, Inside Higher Ed reported. Projections of the final margin varied as late ballots were counted, from 79 Democratic seats to about 83 against 67 for Republicans. Representative Senfronia Thompson, a Houston Democrat first elected in 1972, announced her candidacy for Speaker on election night; the full House will choose the Speaker when the session opens in January 2027. The new officials take office in January.

Why the attorney general race matters for H-1B employers

As attorney general, Paxton built a state-level investigation into suspected H-1B fraud alongside the federal system. His office announced the investigation in January 2026, starting with civil investigative demands to three North Texas businesses, and expanded it on April 30 to nearly 30 North Texas businesses.

"I will not allow the H-1B program to be abused by bad actors seeking to use it as a loophole for allowing foreign nationals to invade Texas."

— Ken Paxton, Texas Attorney General

In its April release, Paxton's office said the businesses were suspected of operating so-called “ghost offices” — falsely representing active operations in order to sponsor foreign workers — and named additional entities including Tekpro IT LLC, Fame PBX LLC, 1st Ranking Technologies LLC, Qubitz Tech Systems LLC, Blooming Clouds LLC, Virat Solutions, Inc., Oak Technologies Inc, Techpath Inc, and Techquency LLC. The demands required documents identifying all employees, records detailing products or services provided, financial statements, and communications related to company operations. Beneficiaries born in India accounted for about 70% of approved H-1B petitions in fiscal 2025, according to U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services figures cited by Bilkul Online. In parallel, Abbott ordered all state agencies to halt H-1B visa applications for state employees through May 2027, according to a Legal 500 analysis.

What changes — and what does not

What changes in January is who decides whether the state scrutiny continues. Whether Johnson continues the H-1B investigations when he takes office is not yet known, Bilkul Online reported, and no statement from Johnson on the demands was reported in the sources reviewed for this article — so employers already under a demand should not assume the inquiry lapses automatically at the handover. As attorney general, Johnson could also reverse the state's position on, or drop entirely, controversial lawsuits Paxton pursued, the Tribune reported.

What does not change is the visa itself. The H-1B program is governed by the Immigration and Nationality Act and federal regulations, and no state has authority to administer or enforce the H-1B program itself, Legal 500 noted. USCIS enforces compliance through site visits and can deny or revoke petitions, and the U.S. Department of Labor enforces wage and working-condition rules, including through its Project Firewall initiative launched in September 2025. Texas enforcement has rested on underlying business conduct under consumer-protection law, without requiring proof of an immigration violation. A new attorney general in Austin therefore cannot change H-1B eligibility, the lottery, or petition fees.

For now, the practical position for Texas H-1B employers is continuity with uncertainty at the state level: keep petition facts aligned with day-to-day operations, keep records complete, and watch for Johnson's first statements after he takes office in January. Indian American candidates also featured in the new House: Democrat Pooja Sethi won the open 47th House District in Austin with about 63% of the vote, according to the Texas Secretary of State's count reported by Bilkul Online.
